events.title: Battle of Marathon
events.text: Athenian and Plataean hoplites defeat the first Persian invasion of Greece, a founding moment in Athenian self-confidence.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.text: The allied Greek fleet destroys much of Xerxes' navy in the narrows off Salamis, turning back the second Persian invasion.

events.title: Peloponnesian War begins
events.text: A 27-year war between the Athenian and Spartan alliances exhausts classical Greece and ends with Athens' defeat in 404 BCE.

events.title: Battle of Gaugamela
events.text: Alexander the Great defeats Darius III, bringing down the Achaemenid Persian Empire and opening the Hellenistic age.

events.title: Death of Alexander
events.text: Alexander dies in Babylon aged 32; his generals (the Diadochi) carve his empire into rival Hellenistic kingdoms.

wikiLang.ja: アレクサンドロス3世の死

events.title: Hannibal crosses the Alps
events.text: In the Second Punic War, Carthage's Hannibal marches an army with war elephants over the Alps to invade Roman Italy.

wikiLang.ja: ハンニバルのアルプス越え

events.title: Destruction of Carthage
events.text: Rome razes Carthage at the end of the Third Punic War (and sacks Corinth the same year), becoming master of the Mediterranean.

events.title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
events.text: Senators stab the dictator Caesar on the Ides of March; the civil wars that follow end the Roman Republic.

wikiLang.ja: ユリウス・カエサルの暗殺

events.title: Battle of Actium
events.text: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at sea; as Augustus he becomes the first Roman emperor in 27 BCE.

events.title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
events.text: Germanic tribes under Arminius destroy three Roman legions, halting Roman expansion east of the Rhine.

wikiLang.ja: トイトブルク森の戦い

events.title: Hadrian's Wall begun
events.text: Emperor Hadrian orders a fortified wall across Britain, marking the empire's turn from expansion to defended frontiers.

events.title: Edict of Milan
events.text: Constantine and Licinius grant religious toleration across the empire, ending the persecution of Christians.

events.title: Constantinople founded
events.text: Constantine dedicates his new capital on the Bosporus; it will be the seat of the Eastern Roman Empire for over a thousand years.

wikiLang.ja: コンスタンティノープル

events.title: Sack of Rome
events.text: Visigoths under Alaric sack Rome, the first time in 800 years the city has fallen to a foreign enemy.

events.title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
events.text: A Roman–Visigothic coalition under Aetius checks Attila's Huns in one of late antiquity's largest battles.

events.title: End of the Western Roman Empire
events.text: Odoacer deposes the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus; the date conventionally marks the end of Roman rule in the West.

events.title: Plague of Justinian
events.text: The first known pandemic of bubonic plague strikes the Mediterranean, killing a large share of the population of Constantinople.

events.title: The Hijra
events.text: Muhammad and his followers migrate from Mecca to Medina; the year becomes the start of the Islamic calendar.

events.title: Battle of the Yarmuk
events.text: Arab Muslim forces defeat the Byzantine army, opening Syria and the Levant to the early caliphate.

events.title: Umayyad conquest of Hispania
events.text: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses from North Africa and defeats the Visigothic king Roderic, beginning nearly eight centuries of al-Andalus.

events.title: Battle of Tours
events.text: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeat an Umayyad raiding army, strengthening Carolingian power in Gaul.

wikiLang.ja: トゥール・ポワティエ間の戦い

events.title: Charlemagne crowned Emperor
events.text: Pope Leo III crowns the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor on Christmas Day, reviving the imperial title in the West.

events.title: Treaty of Verdun
events.text: Charlemagne's grandsons divide the Carolingian Empire into three kingdoms, foreshadowing France and Germany.

events.title: Rurik at Novgorod
events.text: According to the Primary Chronicle, the Varangian Rurik is invited to rule Novgorod, the traditional beginning of the Rus' state.

events.title: Otto I crowned Emperor
events.text: The German king Otto I is crowned emperor, conventionally the founding of the Holy Roman Empire.

wikiLang.ja: オットー1世_(神聖ローマ皇帝)
wikiLang.zh: 奥托一世_(神圣罗马帝国)

events.title: Christianization of Kievan Rus'
events.text: Grand Prince Vladimir adopts Byzantine Orthodox Christianity, shaping the religious culture of Eastern Europe.

events.title: East–West Schism
events.text: Mutual excommunications between papal legates and the Patriarch of Constantinople formalize the split of Catholic and Orthodox churches.

events.title: Battle of Hastings
events.text: William of Normandy defeats Harold II, beginning the Norman conquest of England.

wikiLang.ja: ヘイスティングズの戦い

events.title: Battle of Manzikert
events.text: The Seljuk Turks defeat and capture the Byzantine emperor, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

events.title: Crusaders take Jerusalem
events.text: The First Crusade captures Jerusalem after a siege and massacre, founding the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem.

events.title: Sack of Constantinople
events.text: The Fourth Crusade turns on Constantinople and sacks it, gravely weakening the Byzantine Empire.

wikiLang.ja: コンスタンティノープル包囲戦_(1204年)

events.title: Magna Carta
events.text: Rebel barons force King John to seal a charter limiting royal power, later a touchstone of constitutional government.

events.title: Mongols sack Kyiv
events.text: Batu Khan's Mongol army destroys Kyiv during the invasion of Rus', beginning the era of the Golden Horde.

events.title: Mongols sack Baghdad
events.text: Hulegu's army takes Baghdad and kills the caliph, ending the Abbasid Caliphate's rule from the city.

events.title: Black Death reaches Europe
events.text: Plague arrives on Genoese ships from the Black Sea; within five years it kills perhaps a third or more of Europe's people.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.text: Sultan Mehmed II captures the city, ending the Byzantine Empire; it becomes the Ottoman capital.

wikiLang.ja: コンスタンティノープルの陥落

events.title: Fall of Granada
events.text: Castile and Aragon take the last Muslim state in Iberia; the same year Columbus sails west under the Spanish crown.

events.title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
events.text: Martin Luther challenges the sale of indulgences, sparking the Protestant Reformation.

events.title: First Siege of Vienna
events.text: Suleiman the Magnificent's Ottoman army besieges Vienna but withdraws, marking the limit of Ottoman advance in central Europe for a century.

events.title: Battle of Lepanto
events.text: The Holy League's galleys defeat the Ottoman fleet in the largest naval battle of the age of oared warships.

events.title: Spanish Armada
events.text: Philip II's invasion fleet is beaten off Gravelines and scattered by storms, securing Elizabethan England.

events.title: Thirty Years' War begins
events.text: The Defenestration of Prague triggers a war that devastates the German lands and draws in most of Europe.

events.title: Peace of Westphalia
events.text: Treaties end the Thirty Years' War and the Eighty Years' War, often cited as the origin of the modern system of sovereign states.

wikiLang.ja: ヴェストファーレン条約

events.title: Battle of Vienna
events.text: A relief army led by Jan III Sobieski breaks the Ottoman siege, beginning the Habsburg reconquest of Hungary.

events.title: Saint Petersburg founded
events.text: Peter the Great founds a new capital on the Baltic as Russia's "window to Europe".

wikiLang.ja: サンクトペテルブルク

events.title: French Revolution
events.text: The storming of the Bastille on 14 July becomes the symbol of a revolution that overturns the old regime in France.

events.title: Battle of Austerlitz
events.text: Napoleon defeats Russia and Austria; the Holy Roman Empire is dissolved the following year.

wikiLang.ja: アウステルリッツの戦い

events.title: Napoleon's invasion of Russia
events.text: The Grande Armée reaches a burning Moscow but is destroyed in the winter retreat, breaking Napoleon's power.

events.title: Waterloo and the Congress of Vienna
events.text: Napoleon's final defeat at Waterloo coincides with the Vienna settlement that redraws Europe's map for a generation.

events.title: Revolutions of 1848
events.text: A wave of liberal and national uprisings spreads across Europe; most are suppressed, but serfdom ends in Austria.

events.title: Suez Canal opens
events.text: The canal links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, transforming trade between Europe and Asia.

events.title: German Empire proclaimed
events.text: After victory over France, Wilhelm I is proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors, completing German unification.

events.title: Congress of Berlin
events.text: The great powers revise the Balkan settlement after the Russo-Turkish War; Romania, Serbia and Montenegro become independent.

events.title: Assassination in Sarajevo
events.text: The killing of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sets off the July Crisis and the First World War.

events.title: German invasion of Belgium
events.text: Germany invades neutral Belgium to outflank France under the Schlieffen Plan, bringing Britain into the war.

events.title: Battle of Tannenberg
events.text: German forces encircle and destroy the Russian Second Army in East Prussia within the first month of the war.

wikiLang.ja: タンネンベルクの戦い_(1914年)

events.title: First Battle of the Marne
events.text: French and British counter-attacks halt the German advance on Paris; both sides then dig the trenches of the Western Front.

events.title: First Battle of Ypres
events.text: The 'race to the sea' ends in Flanders; the front line now runs unbroken from the Channel to Switzerland.

events.title: Armenian genocide
events.text: Ottoman authorities arrest Armenian leaders in Constantinople and begin mass deportations and killings; about a million Armenians die.

events.title: Gallipoli landings
events.text: Allied troops land on the Gallipoli peninsula to open the Dardanelles; the campaign fails and is abandoned in January 1916.

events.title: Battles of the Isonzo
events.text: After Italy joins the Allies, it launches the first of twelve costly offensives against Austria-Hungary along the Isonzo.

events.title: Battle of Verdun
events.text: A ten-month battle of attrition between France and Germany becomes a symbol of the Western Front.

events.title: Battle of Jutland
events.text: The largest naval battle of the war; the German fleet inflicts heavier losses but never again challenges British control of the North Sea.

events.title: Brusilov offensive
events.text: Russia's most successful offensive of the war shatters much of the Austro-Hungarian army on the Eastern Front.

events.title: Arab Revolt
events.text: Sharif Hussein of Mecca rises against Ottoman rule with British support, opening a new front in Arabia and the Levant.

events.title: Battle of the Somme
events.text: A British and French offensive whose first day is the bloodiest in British military history; over a million men are killed or wounded.

events.title: Battle of Passchendaele
events.text: A British offensive in Flanders bogs down in rain and mud, gaining a few miles at enormous cost.

wikiLang.ja: パッシェンデールの戦い

events.title: Battle of Caporetto
events.text: Austro-German forces break through the Italian line and drive it back to the Piave river.

events.title: Russian Revolution
events.text: The tsar abdicates in February and the Bolsheviks seize power in October, leading to the Soviet state.

events.title: Capture of Jerusalem
events.text: British forces under Allenby take Jerusalem from the Ottoman Empire during the Sinai and Palestine campaign.

events.title: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
events.text: Soviet Russia leaves the war, ceding the Baltic lands, Poland, Belarus and Ukraine to German control.

wikiLang.ja: ブレスト＝リトフスク条約
wikiLang.zh: 布列斯特-立陶夫斯克條約

events.title: German spring offensive
events.text: Germany's last great offensive gains ground quickly but exhausts its army before American troops arrive in strength.

events.title: Hundred Days Offensive
events.text: Beginning at Amiens, Allied attacks push the German army back across the Western Front in a war of movement.

events.title: Armistice of 11 November
events.text: Germany signs an armistice in a railway carriage at Compiègne; fighting on the Western Front ends at 11 a.m.

wikiLang.ja: ドイツと連合国の休戦協定_(第一次世界大戦)

events.title: Treaty of Versailles
events.text: The peace settlement with Germany, alongside other Paris treaties, dismantles empires and creates new states across Central Europe.

events.title: Republic of Turkey proclaimed
events.text: After the Ottoman Empire's collapse, Mustafa Kemal proclaims the Turkish Republic with its capital at Ankara.

events.title: Anschluss
events.text: Nazi Germany annexes Austria, the first of Hitler's territorial expansions without war.

events.title: Munich Agreement
events.text: Britain, France and Italy allow Germany to annex the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia, the high point of appeasement.

events.title: Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
events.text: Germany and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression pact with a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe between them.

events.title: Second World War begins
events.text: Germany invades Poland on 1 September; Britain and France declare war two days later.

events.title: Winter War
events.text: The Soviet Union invades Finland; Finland resists for over three months before ceding territory.

events.title: Invasion of Denmark and Norway
events.text: Germany occupies Denmark in a day and invades Norway to secure Swedish iron ore and North Atlantic bases.

events.title: Battle of France
events.text: German armour breaks through the Ardennes; the Netherlands, Belgium and France fall within six weeks.

wikiLang.ja: ナチス・ドイツのフランス侵攻

events.title: Dunkirk evacuation
events.text: More than 330,000 British and French soldiers are evacuated by sea from the beaches of Dunkirk.

events.title: Battle of Britain
events.text: The Royal Air Force defeats the Luftwaffe's attempt to win air superiority over Britain, ending invasion plans.

wikiLang.ja: バトル・オブ・ブリテン

events.title: Invasion of Yugoslavia and Greece
events.text: Axis forces overrun Yugoslavia and Greece in a few weeks, securing the Balkans before the attack on the Soviet Union.

events.title: Battle of Crete
events.text: German paratroopers seize Crete in the first large airborne invasion in history, at heavy cost.

events.title: Operation Barbarossa
events.text: Germany and its allies invade the Soviet Union along a front from the Baltic to the Black Sea, the largest invasion in history.

events.title: Siege of Leningrad
events.text: German and Finnish forces cut off Leningrad; the 872-day siege kills around a million civilians, mostly by starvation.

wikiLang.ja: レニングラード包囲戦

events.title: Battle of Moscow
events.text: The German drive on Moscow is stopped at the city's approaches, and a Soviet winter counter-offensive pushes it back.

events.title: Wannsee Conference
events.text: Senior Nazi officials coordinate the 'Final Solution', the systematic murder of Europe's Jews in the Holocaust.

events.title: Battle of Stalingrad
events.text: The Soviet encirclement and destruction of the German Sixth Army marks a turning point of the war in Europe.

wikiLang.ja: スターリングラード攻防戦

events.title: Second Battle of El Alamein
events.text: British Commonwealth forces defeat Rommel's Axis army in Egypt, turning the tide in North Africa.

events.title: Battle of Kursk
events.text: Germany's last major offensive in the East fails; the Red Army takes the strategic initiative for the rest of the war.

events.title: Allied invasion of Sicily
events.text: Allied landings in Sicily lead to Mussolini's fall and Italy's armistice in September.

events.title: D-Day landings
events.text: Allied forces land in Normandy on 6 June, opening a western front against Nazi Germany.

wikiLang.ja: ノルマンディー上陸作戦

events.title: Operation Bagration
events.text: A massive Soviet offensive destroys German Army Group Centre and advances to the Vistula.

events.title: Warsaw Uprising
events.text: The Polish Home Army rises against German occupation; after 63 days the uprising is crushed and the city razed.

events.title: Battle of the Bulge
events.text: Germany's last offensive in the West surprises the Allies in the Ardennes but is defeated within weeks.

events.title: Liberation of Auschwitz
events.text: Soviet troops liberate Auschwitz-Birkenau, where about 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered.

wikiLang.ja: アウシュヴィッツ＝ビルケナウ強制収容所

events.title: Yalta Conference
events.text: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin plan Germany's defeat and occupation and the post-war order in Europe.

events.title: End of the war in Europe
events.text: Berlin falls and Germany surrenders unconditionally in May; Europe is divided into occupation zones.

wikiLang.ja: ヨーロッパ戦勝記念日
wikiLang.zh: 第二次世界大戰歐戰勝利紀念日

events.title: Potsdam Conference
events.text: The victorious Allies settle Germany's occupation zones, the new Polish border and the expulsion of Germans from the East.

events.title: Treaty of Rome
events.text: Six countries found the European Economic Community, forerunner of the European Union.

events.title: Berlin Wall built
events.text: East Germany seals off West Berlin overnight, making the wall the emblem of the Cold War division.

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.text: Border crossings open on 9 November amid peaceful revolutions across Eastern Europe; Germany reunifies in 1990.

events.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
events.text: The USSR breaks into fifteen independent states, redrawing the map of Eastern Europe and the Caucasus.

events.title: European Union founded
events.text: The Maastricht Treaty takes effect, creating the EU and laying the groundwork for the euro.

events.title: EU eastern enlargement
events.text: Ten countries, most formerly in the Soviet sphere, join the European Union in its largest single expansion.
